transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I'm here because I've been losing a lot of weight recently. I've barely been eating any food lately, sometimes just a bite or two a day.
Are you intentionally restricting your food because of a fear of gaining weight, or have you simply lost your appetite and interest in eating?

Yes, I am intentionally restricting my food because I have an overwhelming fear of gaining weight or becoming fat. It's not that I've lost my appetite; I'm just constantly terrified of the scale and feel like I must keep my weight as low as possible. Because of this, I intentionally skip meals and avoid eating to make sure I don't gain anything.
Do you ever have episodes where you eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time, feeling like you cannot control or stop yourself?

No, I never have episodes like that where I lose control and eat a lot. I actually do the exact opposite by strictly limiting my intake and eating as little as possible. I make sure to keep my portions extremely small to avoid gaining any weight.
Even though you have lost a lot of weight, do you still feel that you are overweight or that certain parts of your body are too fat?

Yes, definitely. Even though I've lost a lot of weight, I still feel like I'm overweight and see fat on my body that shouldn't be there. I'm absolutely terrified of gaining any of it back and feel a constant need to lose even more weight.

latest_inference.note: The patient meets all DSM-5 criteria for Anorexia Nervosa, including restriction of energy intake leading to significantly low body weight, an intense fear of gaining weight, and a disturbed body image (perceiving themselves as overweight despite significant weight loss). They deny binge-eating episodes, ruling out Bulimia Nervosa or Binge-Eating Disorder. Therefore, the diagnosis of Anorexia Nervosa is confirmed.
